name: Ampharos Motif Lexicon
purpose: Translate a feeling or narrative into concrete, stageable visual motifs. Each entry maps a meaning to the conceptual metaphors that ground it, the image schema (bodily pattern) underneath, candidate motifs, composition cues, and clichés to avoid.
how_to_use: 1. Parse the brief: name the core feeling AND the narrative arc (state vs. change). 'We won after a hard year' = overcoming + winning, not just winning.
2. Match to entries via `triggers`; pick the closest 1-2 entries. Combine when the brief has an arc (e.g. setback -> comeback).
3. Choose ONE conceptual metaphor as the spine. It decides the axis (up/down, forward/back, inside/outside, light/dark).
4. Pick a motif that fits the brand's world and the medium; adapt it rather than copying the list literally.
5. Choose a staging from `staging` (juxtaposition / fusion / replacement) based on how much work the viewer should do.
6. Apply `composition` cues so direction, light, and color all point the same way as the metaphor.
7. Check `avoid` and the global `cliche_blocklist`. If the motif is one, push one step more specific.
7b. For more source domains on the same idea, read `metanet_metaphors` on the entry, or look up the concept in metanet-index.json; borrow `source_words` as motif seeds.
8. No matching entry? Derive from `image_schemas`: decide which bodily pattern the feeling lives in, then invent a motif on that axis.
9. Note culture: left-to-right progress, color meanings, and gestures are not universal. Flag when the audience isn't Western/LTR.

image_schemas.VERTICALITY: Up/down. Up = more, better, control, happy, status. Down = less, worse, sad, defeated. Composition: placement in frame, camera angle, rising/falling motion.
image_schemas.SOURCE-PATH-GOAL: Start, route, destination. Purposes are destinations; progress is distance covered. Composition: paths, roads, vectors, reading direction.
image_schemas.CONTAINER: Inside/outside/boundary. Belonging, safety, being trapped, emotions held in. Composition: frames within frames, enclosures, doors, thresholds.
image_schemas.FORCE: Compulsion (pushed), blockage (stopped), counterforce (opposed), removal of restraint (released), enablement (helped). Composition: wind, water, pressure, walls, vectors meeting.
image_schemas.BALANCE: Equilibrium vs. precariousness. Stability, fairness, trade-offs, tension. Composition: symmetry, tilt, weight placement.
image_schemas.LINK: Connection between things. Relationships, integration, dependency. Composition: lines, threads, bridges, touching points.
image_schemas.CENTER-PERIPHERY: Core vs. edge. Importance, focus, inclusion/exclusion. Composition: central placement, vignette, radial layouts.
image_schemas.PART-WHOLE: Pieces and wholes. Teams, coherence, fragmentation. Composition: mosaics, puzzles, assemblies, scatter vs. order.
image_schemas.NEAR-FAR: Closeness and distance. Intimacy, similarity, aspiration, isolation. Composition: depth, scale of subject, gaps.
image_schemas.SCALE: Bigger/smaller. Amount, importance, growth, insignificance. Composition: relative size, zoom.
image_schemas.CYCLE: Repeating loops. Seasons, renewal, being stuck, iteration. Composition: circles, loops, sequences returning to start.
image_schemas.LIGHT-DARK: Knowing, hope, goodness, visibility vs. ignorance, fear, sadness. Composition: key light, shadow, exposure, time of day.
image_schemas.FULL-EMPTY: Abundance vs. lack, overflow vs. depletion. Composition: vessels, fill levels, draining.
image_schemas.CONTACT: Touch, grasp, precise meeting. Understanding, control, connection. Composition: hands, points of contact, close-ups.
image_schemas.MERGING / SPLITTING: Coming together vs. breaking apart. Integration, transformation, conflict, choice. Composition: confluences, forks, cracks.
image_schemas.ITERATION: Repeated steps. Persistence, process, momentum. Composition: rhythm, repetition with variation.
image_schemas.SURFACE: What's on top vs. beneath. Calm surfaces, hidden depth, transparency. Composition: water, glass, layers.

staging.note: Adapted from Phillips & McQuarrie's visual rhetoric typology (2004). Ordered from easiest to hardest for the viewer to decode.
staging.juxtaposition: Show the two things side by side (subject + motif, or before + after). Easy to read; good for broad audiences, small sizes, and fast-scroll contexts.
staging.fusion: Merge the subject and motif into one object (a product whose silhouette becomes a summit). More striking; needs clean execution.
staging.replacement: Show only the motif; the viewer supplies the subject from context (a lone podium with the brand color). Most memorable when it lands; riskiest when context is thin.
staging.meaning_operations: Each structure can either CONNECT (A goes with B) or COMPARE (A is like B / A is unlike B). Decide which before staging.

composition_defaults.direction: In LTR contexts, left-to-right reads as forward/future; right-to-left reads as backward/past. Upward diagonals read as positive energy.
composition_defaults.camera: Low angle = power, aspiration. High angle = vulnerability, overview. Eye level = honesty, peer.
composition_defaults.light: Light source = the goal or the truth. Backlight = triumph/hero. Flat light = neutral/stuck. Low-key = drama/fear.
composition_defaults.color: Saturation tracks energy; warmth tracks closeness/positivity; desaturation tracks loss or stasis.
composition_defaults.space: Negative space = calm, freedom, isolation (depends on subject size). Crowding = pressure, abundance, chaos.
composition_defaults._status: Starting hypotheses for non-Prism work only. Prism overrides: color has no meaning; light is the outcome; scale and type rules come from the Prism system.

role_in_prism: Design-time source, not a runtime rule. The Prism visual system (sources/approved-motifs.json, vocabulary, object_system) governs what Ampharos draws. Use this lexicon to propose new feelings and motifs. Write a motif into sources/approved-motifs.json only after a person approves it for reuse. Its literal motifs (podiums, rockets, lighthouses), camera, and color cues do not apply to Prism: Prism is geometric only and colors carry no meaning. Each entry's `prism` field shows which proposed feeling or existing vocabulary covers it.
